title: Orchestrating Topic and Focus in Literary Prose

sections.title: The Full Hungarian Left Periphery
sections.content: In sophisticated Hungarian prose, clauses follow a clear hierarchy before the verb: [Contrastive Topic] -> [Neutral Topic] -> [Quantifiers / Exclusivity Focus / Negation] -> [Conjugated Verb] -> [Detached Preverb + Rest of Clause]. Mastering this template allows you to guide the reader's eye like a camera lens.

sections.title: Reading Kosztolányi's Subtext
sections.content: In 'Pacsirta', Kosztolányi rarely states outright that the parents resent their sacrifices. Instead, he uses focus structures ('Kizárólag Pacsirta kedvéért mondtak le...', 'Csak ekkor döbbent rá...', 'Egyetlen szóval sem vallották be...') to let the tension emerge from what is emphasized and what is negated.

sections.title: Full Information-Structure Template
rows: The train rolled out of the station. (Plot advancement)
[Contrastive Topic] Ákos viszont + [Focus] csak ekkor + [Verb+Preverb] döbbent rá az igazságra.
Ákos, however, realized the truth only then. (Psychological turning point)
[NegFocus] Egyetlen szóval sem + [Verb+Preverb] vallották be a titkot.
Not with a single word did they confess the secret. (Emphatic suppression)
Solely for her sake did they give up everything. (Hidden resentment)

items.spanish: Ami a szülőket illeti, ők egyetlen szóval sem vallották be a megkönnyebbülésüket.
items.english: As for the parents, not with a single word did they admit their relief.

items.spanish: A peronon még sírtak, a vendéglőben viszont már a régi dalokat hallgatták.
items.english: On the platform they were still crying; in the restaurant, however, it was already the old songs they were listening to.

items.spanish: Nem a lányuk hiánya, hanem a hirtelen szabadság ijesztette meg őket.
items.english: It was not their daughter's absence, but the sudden freedom that frightened them.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: When translating B2 Hungarian prose into English, ask yourself which word stands immediately before the verb—that word is the emotional pivot of the sentence.
